title: Did you know… Peter had to overcome personal bias to preach to Gentiles?
paragraphs: Did you know… Peter had to overcome personal bias to preach to Gentiles?
He walked with Jesus… yet still struggled with people.
Yes—Peter the Apostle carried bias in his heart.
In Acts of the Apostles 10, Peter receives a vision—unclean animals lowered from heaven. A voice says, “Kill and eat.”
Because in his mind, “unclean” people were off-limits too.
It was about who he believed deserved God.
Then enters Cornelius—a Gentile, an outsider, the kind Peter was trained to avoid.
Yet God was already moving in Cornelius’ life.
And that’s where everything breaks open.
Peter steps into Cornelius’ house—something he never would’ve done before—and says:
“I now realize how true it is that God does not show favoritism…” (Acts 10:34)

The same Peter who once said, “I will never…”
Is now standing in a Gentile home saying, “God shows no partiality.”
Because the Gospel doesn’t just save us from sin.
It confronts the hidden prejudices we protect.
The people we silently rank beneath us.
Through His blood, both Jew and Gentile are brought near (Ephesians 2:13).
And here’s the truth that hits hard:
You can walk with Jesus… and still carry bias.
But you cannot follow Him deeply without letting Him break it.
Because the cross is level ground.
At the foot of Christ, no one stands higher.

Ask the Lord:
“Who have I kept at a distance that You are calling me to love?”
